newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Grand Canyon air tour operators sue FAA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Grand Canyon air tour operators sue FAA.

text.p: Thirteen companies that conduct air sightseeing tours of the Grand Canyon Monday said they had sued the Federal Aviation Administration over its new rules to limit flights over the national park to reduce noise.

The FAA last week announced rules to reduce allowable air space and impose dusk-to-dawn curfews for the tours which the Interior Department said were generating an intolerable din that marred the canyon experience.

"The coalition (of companies) has moved quickly to challenge the FAA rules because air tour operators are facing a May 1, 1997 compliance date for these new and unjustified restrictions," Donald Elliott, the coalition's attorney, said.
Dan Anderson, president of the United States Air Tour Association, said the new rules could put a number of small operators out of business.
The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.
